chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, who said: He narrated to us Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: He narrated to us Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He loves a servant, takes (deaths) the child most beloved to him.

key_terms.قَبَضَ: To take possession of, to cause to die

ai.seo_question: What is the sign that Allah loves a servant according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing a specific sign of divine love (hubb ilahi) as the death of the servant's most beloved child. This concept is central to Shia theology, where bereavement is viewed not merely as a trial but as a means of spiritual purification and elevation, reflecting the principle that Allah removes what is most dear to test and refine the believer's attachment to Him. The chain of transmission underscores the reliability of this tradition within the Usuli school, linking it directly to the Imams' teachings on the wisdom behind divine decrees.
